title: Generalized Cooperative Delegation Credential
description: Define the authorizations, duties, and constraints of a delegate who receives delegated authority. Version 5.0 grounds the credential in agency law (this.i @3w3rkmt3) and separates three jobs: the constraints container is the only machine gate, the rules bind only the parties who issued, admitted or accepted the credential, and toward relying parties the rules state conditions of reliance and defer to applicable law. The facet names roles rather than liability: liableParty is gone, and principal and agentOfRecord name the party bound by the delegate's acts and the legal person who acts through the delegate, beside durable and a digest of the principal's own grant text (grantText); the facet is closed. Reserved powers are conferred only by name (constraints.reservedPowers), and humanReview names who may approve (constraints.reviewers). Optional edges name the parent credential of a sub-delegation, a gcd-disclosure made by the agent of record before the grant, and evidence of how the grant was executed; acceptance is a separate gcd-acceptance credential issued after it. The rules are complete and supersede every earlier version, add an optional governing law, and carry seven baseline duties, six of them owed by the delegate in a new prose duty shape. Version 4.0 names the targets of acts (constraints.targets): the objects a delegate may act on, or who may designate them, so a delegate cannot be made a confused deputy by a stranger who chooses where its authority lands; acts and targets are one constraint, so a credential that grants acts must also say which targets. Version 3.1 admits custom keys inside the constraints container and inside a duty, so an issuer can express a constraint or obligation the standard fields do not cover; the fail-closed rule on an unrecognized constraint key is unchanged, but it is now enforced by the verifier rather than by schema validation. Version 3.0 adopts the ACDC v2 envelope (acm/JSON: rd replaces ri, message type t, most-compact-form SAIDs). Version 2.0 organized the attributes block into named containers (facet, constraints) with sibling voiding (terminatingEvents) and outbound-disclosure (disclosables) axes, and first-classed duties in the rules block.
$comment: These credentials have no required edges block. When the e block is present it carries an I2I issuer edge that chains the issuer's identity to another credential, and optionally a parent edge (required by the subDelegation rule whenever the issuer's own authority is delegated), a disclosure edge to a gcd-disclosure, and an execution edge to evidence of how the grant was made. Acceptance by an agent of record is not an edge here, because the acceptor does not sign the GCD; it is a gcd-acceptance credential that points at this one.

t.description: Message type. Optional; an ACDC JSON message without it is of type acm.

rd.description: Registry SAID: the SAID of the registry inception (rip) event of the issuer's credential-status registry. Required: a GCD is authority evidence, and secure discovery of its revocation registry outweighs correlation minimization here.

i.description: AID of the delegate (the issuee) who receives the delegated authority. When the delegate is also a KERI cooperative-delegated AID of the issuer, this is the AID as it appears in the delegator's interaction event — but GCD does not require a KERI cooperative-delegation binding; it documents delegated authority for any issuer-to-delegate relationship.

gfw.description: A SAID that identifies a governance framework that adds richer semantics to the role field and any custom constraints present in this credential. The SAID identifies a JSON rules block that supplements the generic rules in the rules block (r field). The location of this additional rules block is assumed to be published somewhere that stakeholders know. A governance framework may narrow the authority the constraints grant but never widens it, and may reserve further powers but never release one. When defined, a verifier MUST NOT impute a delegator's approval of delegated authority to a delegate without understanding and enforcing the rules of these extra rules.

facet.description: The relationship facet: descriptive metadata about the delegation relationship, orthogonal to the enabling constraints. It names roles, not liability, which is a conclusion for law to reach from the facts. A verifier MAY ignore the facet for the raw authorization decision; only the constraints container gates, together with the acceptance, sub-delegation and human-review conditions the rules state. This container is CLOSED as of 5.0.0: an unknown key is rejected, so tooling that still writes the 4.0.0 liableParty cannot carry it forward with its old, ambiguous meaning.

role.description: A string that names a profile of duties and corresponding authorizations that the delegator intends to confer on the delegate. When gfw is defined and specifies formal semantics for this role, the role may narrow the authority the constraints grant, or add constraints a GCD credential is otherwise incapable of modeling, but never widens that authority or confers a reserved power. When gfw is NOT defined, this field is a simple descriptive label with no enforceable meaning, and no party is justified in expecting it to convey any constraints.

relationType.description: Whose interest the delegated act serves, and the subject's standing. delegation: the delegate acts for a self-sovereign delegator. guardianship: the delegate acts for a non-sovereign dependent. controllership: the delegate acts over a thing. stewardship: guardianship's fiduciary posture applied to a domain the steward runs as their own.

principal.description: AID of the principal: the party bound by the delegate's authorized acts and on whose account they are taken (Restatement (Third) of Agency §1.01, §6.01, §7.03). Absent, it defaults to the issuer; set it only when the two differ, as when an officer issues for a company or a court issues for an individual subject to guardianship. Who is liable for an act is for the law to decide, not this field.

agentOfRecord.description: AID of the agent of record: the legal person the principal appoints as agent and who acts through the delegate, such as the company that operates an AI delegate. It is an agent because the principal appointed it and it assented by issuing a gcd-acceptance, and it owes the duties whose bearer is the delegate. A delegate that is a legal person acting for itself is named here as its own agent of record. Absent only when the principal uses its own software as the delegate, which is then the principal's own instrument. When present, a verifier denies every act until it is shown a matching gcd-acceptance, and this credential must carry a disclosure edge. Liability is for the law to decide, not this field.

presentsAs.description: The facet-AID the act is presented under to a counterparty (for example, an 'Office of the CEO' facet an assistant is delegated into). Presenting-as without this granted capability is impersonation. The signer is always the actor's own key; presentsAs governs only the presented identity, not the signature.

exerciseMode.description: Which of the two independent authorities this credential confers. act: authority-to-act only (the delegate performs gated acts itself). authorize: authority-to-authorize only -- the pure delegator, with an empty set of goals, who may sanction others' gated acts but performs none itself. both: authority-to-act and authority-to-authorize.

durable.description: The principal's stated intent that the authority survive the principal's loss of capacity. Absent means false, the common-law default (Restatement (Third) of Agency §3.08). Whether it does survive is for the law governing the relationship; the termination rule gives this field effect only where that law does.

grantText.description: A digest of the words the principal approved as the grant, so a party or tribunal shown the text can check that it is the one this credential was issued on. The text itself is not inlined, because a GCD discloses every attribute to every verifier. Ambiguous terms are read against the party that drafted them, so the drafter is named.

digest.description: The CESR-encoded Blake3-256 digest of the grant text's canonical form under canon.

canon.description: The canonicalization applied to the text before it is digested. Fixed to the exact identifier cqt3.17 (Canonical Quoted Text 3.17), which that specification requires be bound in whatever is signed.

constraints.description: The enabling 'may': the allow-list dimensions that a stranger-verifier gates on. Within a field, values are ORed (any match satisfies that field); across fields they are ANDed (every present field must be satisfied). An absent field is unconstrained in that dimension. acts and targets are two keys for ONE dimension, act space located by (effect, state-kind, target): with neither present it is unconstrained, and acts without targets is invalid (dependentRequired), so an issuer who limits what kind of act may be done must also say on what, or declare that any target will do. Custom keys are allowed here (additionalProperties is true as of 3.1.0), so an issuer can express a constraint the standard fields do not cover; such a key takes its semantics from the governance framework named in gfw, and useStdIfPossible obliges an issuer to prefer a standard field wherever one fits. This container remains FAIL-CLOSED, but the obligation runs to the verifier, not to schema validation: a verifier that does not understand a key it finds here MUST assume that constraint is unmet and MUST deny. Admitting a key is not vouching for it, and validating against this schema is not an authorization decision. This container is the only part of the credential a verifier evaluates to permit or deny an act, together with the acceptance, sub-delegation and human-review conditions the rules state; the rules, any ancestor credential and applicable law may further limit the authority a delegate has in law.

goals.description: Array of Hyperledger Aries goal codes (https://bit.ly/3ROeww6) that describe purpose-seeking behaviors that are valid for the delegate. Goal codes are matched as if they contained a trailing .* wildcard; that is, the "sell" goal code matches "sell.consumer" and "sell.enterprise". This field is case-insensitive.

acts.description: The set of (effect, state-kind) POINTS this delegate may act on — the enabling 'may' over the act grid. Each entry is one point, written 'effect state-kind' (e.g. 'create commitment'), or a one-sided brace enumeration naming several kinds for one effect ('observe {info, record}') or several effects for one kind ('{create, modify} record'); items inside braces separate on one or more commas or spaces. effect is one of observe, create, modify, preserve, destroy; state-kind is one of info, record, commitment, authority, resource, relationship — the two axes of one coordinate, neither meaningful alone. An act is authorized only if EVERY (effect, state-kind) point it occupies is covered here. The gate (auto/rule/human) an act must clear is DERIVED per act from its points and its target via the governance framework (gfw), not enumerated here. A pure delegator (exerciseMode authorize) omits this field, having an empty act surface. Two-sided braces and wildcards are intentionally not allowed. acts and targets are one constraint: a credential that carries acts MUST carry targets, which names the objects these points may be exercised on (see targets).

targets.description: The objects the delegate may act on, or whose designation of them the delegate may act on -- the defense against a confused deputy, where a stranger chooses the target and the delegate supplies the authority. An OR-set: an act whose target is contained by SOME entry passes this field. Matching is EXACT over the kind's canonical form, because any loose comparison is a bypass. A target whose kind no entry names matches nothing, and an entry whose kind the verifier does not know matches nothing; a verifier that finds no entry containing the act's target MUST deny. An act whose target the grant itself fixes (a duty-driven act) passes only where the governance framework or the protocol binding says that act kind carries no target. Required whenever acts is present. Bounded: at most 1024 entries, 30 act points per entry of at most 128 characters each, 64 designator AIDs, a 64-character kind and a 256-character id.

oneOf.description: A NAMED target: designation at grant time. The principal chose this object in advance, so a stranger checks an act's target against the credential alone, with no evidence about who asked for the act.

kind.description: The kind of object, which fixes its canonical form and its containment rule. Standard kinds: aid (any qb64 identifier prefix KERI can derive: a basic Ed25519, ECDSA or Ed448 key, or a self-addressing digest) and said (any qb64 KERI digest, 256 or 512 bits), both matched by equality, iban (an ISO 13616 account number in electronic format -- no spaces, uppercase -- matched by equality; a verifier MUST also check its check digits, which this schema cannot). A governance framework (gfw) may define other kinds as lowercase dotted names. A verifier that does not know a kind MUST treat the entry as matching nothing.

id.description: The object, in its kind's canonical form. The pattern admits only the qb64 derivation codes an aid or said can carry, with zero pad bits; a verifier MUST still parse the value as qb64 with a CESR parser, which a pattern cannot fully do.

acts.description: Narrows, and never widens: an act on this entry's targets must be covered by these points AND by constraints.acts when that is present. Same syntax as constraints.acts.

oneOf.description: A DESIGNATOR entry: designation at act time. Any target of this kind is covered if the party who named it in the act's request satisfies designatedBy. The act must then carry the signed request that named the target, so the verifier learns who designated it.

kind.description: The kind of object, which fixes its canonical form and its containment rule. Standard kinds: aid (any qb64 identifier prefix KERI can derive: a basic Ed25519, ECDSA or Ed448 key, or a self-addressing digest) and said (any qb64 KERI digest, 256 or 512 bits), both matched by equality, iban (an ISO 13616 account number in electronic format -- no spaces, uppercase -- matched by equality; a verifier MUST also check its check digits, which this schema cannot). A governance framework (gfw) may define other kinds as lowercase dotted names. A verifier that does not know a kind MUST treat the entry as matching nothing. On a designator entry only, '*' means every kind.

designatedBy.description: Whose designation of a target the delegate may act on. 'any': anyone's, which is the most permissive stance and must be declared because it is never the default. {aids}: a target named in a request signed by one of these AIDs (the principal, or someone the principal names). {proof}: a target named by a party who satisfies the proof request with this SAID -- the same kind of object constraints.proofs references. The designator must have signed the designating request itself; a designation relayed through another party does not count.

acts.description: Narrows, and never widens: an act on this entry's targets must be covered by these points AND by constraints.acts when that is present. Same syntax as constraints.acts.

reservedPowers.description: The reserved powers this credential confers, each by name, from a closed vocabulary aligned to UPOAA §201(a) plus channel redirection and self-dealing; the reservedPowers rule defines each one. Absent means none is conferred: a reserved power is never conferred by the breadth of a grant, by a role, by a governance framework, or by the absence of this field, and a verifier MUST deny an act it can classify as a reserved power whose code is not listed here; whether an act is one is otherwise for applicable law, and a verifier's failure to classify an act confers nothing. A governance framework may reserve further powers but never release one. Narrowing, suspending or revoking a grant is never a reserved power.

domains.description: Array of authorization-domain identifiers that scope where (in which authorization domain) the delegated authority applies. A domain is an issuer-defined namespace label; it is case-sensitive and compared verbatim.

jurisdictions.description: Array of ISO 3166-1 alpha2 codes for countries and possibly ISO 3166-2 codes for regions or provinces. These codes enumerate legal jurisdictions where the delegator MAY accept a delegate's actions as transferring legal obligations to the delegator. Note the use of the word "MAY". Even if all other constraints are met, a delegator is not committing to accept legal responsibility for arbitrary actions of a delegate by enumerating jurisdictions here. Acceptance of legal responsibility needs a custom governance framework. Rather, the delegator is communicating that, if a verifier requires legal recourse, the verifier MUST NOT impute the delegator's approval of delegated authority to the delegate in jurisdictions that do not match this list. Verifiers that do not require legal recourse MAY ignore this field. This field is case-sensitive. This is not the law that governs the relationship among the parties, which the rules' governingLaw entry names.

physGeos.description: Array of ISO 3166-1 alpha2 codes for countries (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) and possibly ISO 3166-2 codes for regions or provinces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2). These codes identify where a physically present delegate MAY be located while exercising their delegated authority. Location MUST be determined by a strong test of physical presence (e.g., by a closed-circuit camera, by a human doing identity verification). A verifier MUST NOT impute the delegator's approval of delegated authority to the delegate unless they have solid proof of physical presence in a matching location. This field is case-sensitive.

virtGeos.description: Array of ISO 3166-1 alpha2 codes for countries and possibly ISO 3166-2 codes for regions or provinces. These codes identify where a possibly remote (virtually present) delegate MAY be located while validly exercising their delegated authority. Location is loosely determined in ways familiar on the web today (e.g., by internet geolocation, by cell phone triangulation). Because such methods often lack strong assurance, this constraint may be weaker than physGeos. This field is case-sensitive.

icals.description: Array of iCalendar objects or object fragments, as defined in [RFC 5545](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545) and its subsequent updates. Each item characterizes (in full, or preferably, in part) an event profile in which the delegate MAY exercise their delegated authority, subject to other constraints. The iCal properties that establish GCD constraints are: DTSTART, DTEND, RRULE, RDATE, EXDATE, and LOCATION. All other properties, including BEGIN and END, SHOULD be suppressed for brevity and MUST be ignored by all parties when evaluating constraints. DTSTART and DTEND establish timing constraints; RRULE and RDATE and EXDATE establish recurrence rules and exceptions. LOCATION is a semicolon-delimited list of URLs that give context to the event -- for example, links to a web meeting or a chat room, and an event is considered to have a matching location if it takes place in one of these locations. When a verifier tests a candidate event against items in the icals array, all constraining properties of the item must match the candidate event to produce a match, except that the candidate event does not have to recur; it only has to occur at a time that the recurrence rule would allow. This field is case-insensitive.

monetaryLimit.description: Constrains the financial stakes of the delegated action; the delegate can act only in contexts where a financial value less than this value is at stake. Value is a string containing a magnitude, then a space, then a currency-like unit: an ISO 4217 currency symbol, a cryptocurrency abbreviation, or a brief single-token commodity-value symbol with obvious meaning. This field is money-locked: it is NOT a general 'stakes' quantity. Non-money or unquantifiable stakes route to the governance gate, not here.

protos.description: Array of strings that each name a protocol followed by one or more formally named roles in that protocol. The delegate is authorized to participate in the named protocols in any of the named roles, subject to other constraints. Protocols that are defined in a formal standard MUST be identified by the standard org and number, if possible (e.g., HTTP/2 is identified by "rfc7540", and a credit card protocol "iso8353"). In some cases, a semver-style number is used instead of a standard number (as with the EMV credit card protocol, which is represented with "emv3.0"). DIDComm protocols use PIURIs (https://bit.ly/474pyRZ). The protocol name is followed by a colon, and then a comma-separated list of role names. This field is case-insensitive. Comparisons of strings in this constraint field MUST ignore whitespace and punctuation except the punctuation in version numbers.

proofs.description: Array of SAIDs that each identify an IPEX proof request. The delegate is allowed to exercise delegated authority only if at least one proof request in the array is satisfied (the array is an OR). An AND of proofs is expressed as a single composite proof request, so this array never needs AND semantics.

validFrom.description: Time after which delegated authority becomes active. Including this constraint allows a delegator to issue a GCD credential before -- possibly long before -- the authority becomes active. This field is somewhat like the icals DTSTART. However, icals SHOULD be used to list multiple valid time ranges; this field SHOULD be used to define a single absolute floor.

validUntil.description: Time at which delegated authority expires. Including this constraint allows a delegator to issue a GCD credential that lapses naturally without having to be revoked. This field is somewhat like the icals DTEND. However, icals SHOULD be used to list multiple valid time ranges; this field SHOULD be used to define a single absolute ceiling. A GCD that carries terminatingEvents MUST also carry a validUntil, so a never-fired termination signal cannot leave authority alive forever.

humanReview.description: Instructions for constraints that must be evaluated by a human. An act this field covers is gated on an approval that a reviewer named or qualified in reviewers has signed before the act and that identifies the act by its digest, so the gate is checkable open-loop; the quality of the review is a duty under the humanReview rule, not part of the gate. Any GCD credential that has this field MUST carry reviewers, and MUST NOT be verified without such an approval.

reviewers.description: Who may sign the approvals that humanReview requires. An OR-set: an approval passes if its signer satisfies SOME entry. {aids}: a reviewer whose AID is listed. {proof}: a reviewer who satisfies the proof request with this SAID, the same kind of object constraints.proofs references. Required whenever humanReview is present. Bounded at 64 entries of at most 64 AIDs each.

terminatingEvents.description: Voiding polarity: an array of SAIDs that each identify a proof request for an attested event whose occurrence VOIDS this delegated authority. ANY one firing ends the authority (the array is an OR of termination conditions). These are proof-shaped attested facts, not live predicates, so the credential's meaning stays static and any two verifiers replay to the same result. A credential that carries terminatingEvents MUST also carry constraints.validUntil as a hard backstop.

disclosables.description: Outbound-disclosure axis: an array of credential-SCHEMA SAIDs that the delegate MAY reveal about its principal while acting under this delegation. Absent means unconstrained; present means an allow-list at schema granularity. Intra-credential selective disclosure remains ACDC's job.

issuer.description: Edge credential that proves the identity of the issuer.

n.description: SAID of a credential that proves the identity of the issuer

s.description: SAID of credential schema that proves the identity of the issuer

o.description: Operator indicating issuer AID of this ACDC MUST be the Issuee AID of the node this Edge points to.

parent.description: The GCD under which the issuer holds the authority it delegates here. Required by the subDelegation rule whenever the issuer's own authority is delegated, and the parent must list substitute among its reserved powers; authority under this credential is then the intersection of its constraints and reserved powers with those of every ancestor. The absence of this edge is the issuer's representation that it holds the authority in its own right, not proof of it. Operator I2I: this credential's issuer is the parent's issuee. The parent's schema is not pinned, because a GCD cannot name its own SAID; s, when present, MUST be the SAID of a GCD schema, and a verifier MUST deny if it cannot obtain and verify every ancestor.

s.description: SAID of the parent's schema, which MUST be a GCD schema

o.description: Operator indicating the issuer AID of this ACDC MUST be the issuee AID of the parent.

disclosure.description: The gcd-disclosure the agent of record issued to the principal before this credential. Required whenever facet.agentOfRecord is present. Issuing this credential is evidence of the principal's consent to the compensation and conflicts that disclosure states, and to nothing else (the disclosure rule). Operator NI2I, because the disclosure's issuee is the principal, which differs from this credential's issuer when principal is set; a verifier checks that the disclosure's issuer is the agentOfRecord and its issuee is the principal, or the issuer when principal is absent.

o.description: Operator: no issuer-to-issuee constraint; the edge description states the parties a verifier checks.

execution.description: Evidence of how the grant was made: a notarization, a witnessed recording, a face-to-face attestation. This is where evidence of the principal's understanding and capacity belongs, attested by someone other than the issuer. Operator NI2I, because the attester's issuee need not be this credential's issuer.

n.description: SAID of the credential that attests the execution

oneOf.const: In these rules, the principal is the party named in the principal field, or the issuer if that field is absent; the delegate is the issuee; the agent of record is the legal person named in the agentOfRecord field; and a relying party is anyone who relies on this credential as evidence of authority. These rules are complete. They supersede every earlier version of the rules of this credential type, and no clause of an earlier version applies to this credential.

l.const: In these rules, the principal is the party named in the principal field, or the issuer if that field is absent; the delegate is the issuee; the agent of record is the legal person named in the agentOfRecord field; and a relying party is anyone who relies on this credential as evidence of authority. These rules are complete. They supersede every earlier version of the rules of this credential type, and no clause of an earlier version applies to this credential.

oneOf.const: The issuer is bound by these rules by issuing this credential. The agent of record is bound by issuing an acceptance of this credential. Any person that, with notice of these rules, controls the delegate's keys or directs the delegate's acts under this credential thereby undertakes the duties whose bearer is the delegate, as if it were the agent of record; this undertaking does not cure the absence of a required acceptance, and naming a person does not by itself bind that person. Duties whose bearer is the delegate are owed by the agent of record. These rules are made for the benefit of the principal, who may enforce them whether or not it issued this credential. No other agreement narrows these duties unless the principal signed it and it identifies this credential. A relying party is bound only by an agreement it has separately made; otherwise, the clauses that concern relying parties state the conditions on which this credential may be relied on and impose no obligation on them. Software is bound by nothing.

l.const: The issuer is bound by these rules by issuing this credential. The agent of record is bound by issuing an acceptance of this credential. Any person that, with notice of these rules, controls the delegate's keys or directs the delegate's acts under this credential thereby undertakes the duties whose bearer is the delegate, as if it were the agent of record; this undertaking does not cure the absence of a required acceptance, and naming a person does not by itself bind that person. Duties whose bearer is the delegate are owed by the agent of record. These rules are made for the benefit of the principal, who may enforce them whether or not it issued this credential. No other agreement narrows these duties unless the principal signed it and it identifies this credential. A relying party is bound only by an agreement it has separately made; otherwise, the clauses that concern relying parties state the conditions on which this credential may be relied on and impose no obligation on them. Software is bound by nothing.

oneOf.const: A verifier permits an act only if all of the following hold, and denies if any is missing, unrecognized or unverifiable: every constraint in the constraints container is satisfied; where the role field is present or the constraints container holds a key that is not a standard field, the verifier implements the governance framework named in gfw and that framework's semantics are satisfied; the act is not one the verifier classifies as a reserved power that the reservedPowers constraint does not list; where the agentOfRecord field is present, the disclosure edge references a disclosure issued by the agent of record to the principal, and an acceptance issued by the agent of record that identifies this credential is shown, each with a signature that verifies against its issuer's key state; where the parent edge is present, every ancestor credential is shown, verifies and is satisfied, and the immediate parent lists substitute among its reserved powers; where the humanReview constraint is present, an approval that identifies the act is shown, signed by a reviewer the reviewers constraint names or qualifies, with a signature that verifies against that reviewer's key state; no terminating event is shown; and the credential chain, revocation status and key state verify. This list is exhaustive, and no other clause of these rules adds a condition a verifier checks, though any clause may limit authority in law. A successful verification establishes only that these conditions held when checked, not that the delegate had authority in law.

l.const: A verifier permits an act only if all of the following hold, and denies if any is missing, unrecognized or unverifiable: every constraint in the constraints container is satisfied; where the role field is present or the constraints container holds a key that is not a standard field, the verifier implements the governance framework named in gfw and that framework's semantics are satisfied; the act is not one the verifier classifies as a reserved power that the reservedPowers constraint does not list; where the agentOfRecord field is present, the disclosure edge references a disclosure issued by the agent of record to the principal, and an acceptance issued by the agent of record that identifies this credential is shown, each with a signature that verifies against its issuer's key state; where the parent edge is present, every ancestor credential is shown, verifies and is satisfied, and the immediate parent lists substitute among its reserved powers; where the humanReview constraint is present, an approval that identifies the act is shown, signed by a reviewer the reviewers constraint names or qualifies, with a signature that verifies against that reviewer's key state; no terminating event is shown; and the credential chain, revocation status and key state verify. This list is exhaustive, and no other clause of these rules adds a condition a verifier checks, though any clause may limit authority in law. A successful verification establishes only that these conditions held when checked, not that the delegate had authority in law.

oneOf.const: Issuers agree to express a constraint in a standard field wherever one reasonably fits, rather than in a custom field or in prose, so that a verifier can rely on the absence of a standard field to mean that the credential imposes no constraint in that dimension. The absence of a standard field never confers a reserved power.

l.const: Issuers agree to express a constraint in a standard field wherever one reasonably fits, rather than in a custom field or in prose, so that a verifier can rely on the absence of a standard field to mean that the credential imposes no constraint in that dimension. The absence of a standard field never confers a reserved power.

oneOf.const: A role has no enforceable meaning unless the gfw field names a governance framework that defines it. A governance framework, and any role or custom constraint it defines, may narrow the authority the constraints grant but never widens it.

l.const: A role has no enforceable meaning unless the gfw field names a governance framework that defines it. A governance framework, and any role or custom constraint it defines, may narrow the authority the constraints grant but never widens it.

oneOf.const: Within its constraints and subject to these rules, every ancestor credential and applicable law, this credential is the issuer's representation, made for the principal where they differ, that the delegate has the authority it describes. Where the issuer differs from the principal, the credential alone does not prove that the issuer was authorized to issue it. Outside its constraints, no representation is made and the credential alone does not establish authority. Admissibility, weight, apparent authority, ratification and the protection of good-faith reliance are for applicable law.

l.const: Within its constraints and subject to these rules, every ancestor credential and applicable law, this credential is the issuer's representation, made for the principal where they differ, that the delegate has the authority it describes. Where the issuer differs from the principal, the credential alone does not prove that the issuer was authorized to issue it. Outside its constraints, no representation is made and the credential alone does not establish authority. Admissibility, weight, apparent authority, ratification and the protection of good-faith reliance are for applicable law.

oneOf.const: Nothing in these rules waives, narrows or displaces a right or duty that applicable law makes mandatory, and where a clause conflicts with mandatory law, the law governs. Nothing in this credential confers authority for an act that the law requires the principal to perform in person or in a particular form. If a clause is unenforceable, the remaining clauses continue to apply, and the gap is filled as the governing law provides. Rights and obligations that accrued before authority ended survive its end.

oneOf.const: A reserved power is conferred only where the reservedPowers constraint names it. It is never conferred by the breadth of a grant, by a role, by a governance framework, by an approval, or by the absence of a constraint. The reserved powers are: substitute, to confer, transfer or substitute authority over the principal's affairs, including appointing a sub-delegate or a substitute; redirectNotice, to change, redirect or suspend any channel through which the principal receives notice of, or exercises control over, the principal's affairs, including the principal's addresses and contact details held by others; selfDeal, to take an act in which the delegate, the agent of record, or a person related to either acts on the other side or receives a benefit, other than compensation disclosed before this credential was issued; gift, to make a gift; trust, to create, amend, revoke or terminate a trust; survivorship, to create or change rights of survivorship; beneficiary, to create or change a beneficiary designation; waiveAnnuity, to waive the principal's right to be a beneficiary of a joint and survivor annuity; fiduciaryPowers, to exercise fiduciary powers that the principal has authority to delegate; and disclaim, to disclaim property, including a power of appointment. Whether an act is a reserved power is for applicable law, and a verifier's failure to classify an act as one confers nothing. A governance framework may reserve further powers but may not release any. Narrowing, suspending or revoking this credential, or any other act by which the principal reduces authority it has granted, is never a reserved power.

oneOf.const: A credential whose issuer holds its authority by delegation must name the exact credential under which it holds it in its parent edge, and that parent must list substitute among its reserved powers. Authority under such a credential is the intersection of its constraints and reserved powers with those of every ancestor, and ends when any ancestor's authority ends. The absence of a parent edge is the issuer's representation that it holds the authority in its own right, not proof of it. A delegate that appoints a sub-delegate remains answerable to the principal for it.

oneOf.const: Where the agentOfRecord field is present, no act is authorized under this credential until the agent of record has issued an acceptance that identifies itself and this credential by its exact identifier. An acceptance is unqualified and is given after this credential is issued; a qualified acceptance is no acceptance. A delegate that is a legal person acting for itself is named as its own agent of record. Omitting the agentOfRecord field is the issuer's representation that the principal itself operates the delegate, in which case no acceptance is required and the principal answers for the delegate's acts as its own.

oneOf.const: Where the agentOfRecord field is present, this credential must reference, in its disclosure edge, a disclosure issued by the agent of record to the principal before this credential. oneOf.const: As between the parties, authority under this credential ends as the law governing their relationship provides, including on the death, loss of capacity or dissolution of a principal and on the dissolution of an agent of record. The durable field records the principal's intent and has the effect that law gives it. These rules do not define incapacity. A terminating event is a credential that satisfies a proof request listed in the terminatingEvents field; a terminating event ends authority for a verifier only when it is shown to that verifier, so the issuer's duty to revoke, and the validUntil constraint, remain the backstops. Whether an act taken in good faith, without notice that authority had ended, binds the principal is for the governing law. Termination and revocation are prospective and do not undo acts completed while authority existed. The agent of record may renounce this delegation by notice to the principal, which ends its authority prospectively. The duties of confidentiality and of keeping and producing records survive the end of authority.

oneOf.const: Where the humanReview constraint is present, an act is gated on an approval that a reviewer named or qualified in the reviewers constraint has signed before the act and that identifies the act by its digest. A reviewer must have authority to refuse, access to the evidence on which the act rests, and time to consider it; an approval given without these breaches the delegate's duties even though it satisfies the gate. Where the principal is an individual able to take part, review means the principal's own decision, with whatever support the principal chooses.

oneOf.const: Where the grantText field is present, a text that matches its digest under its stated canonicalization is evidence of the words the principal approved. Neither the digest nor the drafter proves the principal's receipt, approval, capacity or assent. The text never widens the constraints, though it may evidence a narrower grant. Its interpretation is for applicable law, and the agent of record preserves the text and evidence of its approval.

governingLaw.description: governingLaw Clause. Its detail form may also carry the governing-law entry itself: law, the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 or ISO 3166-2 codes of the law that governs these rules and the relationship among the parties bound by them. Present only in the detail form, and optional; it never gates an act, which is why it is here and not in the constraints container. No forum is named, because several model acts void pre-dispute forum and arbitration clauses.

oneOf.const: If the governingLaw entry is present, it names the law that governs these rules and the relationship among the parties bound by them. It does not displace protection that mandatory law gives a consumer, an employee or a person subject to guardianship, and it does not govern the authority of a representative toward, or the effect of an act on, a relying party that has not agreed to it.

law.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, or ISO 3166-2 codes for a subdivision, naming the governing law. Case-sensitive.

oneOf.const: Where duties conflict, a duty of higher priority outranks one of lower priority, except that a conflict involving loyalty, confidentiality or escalate is never resolved by priority and must be referred to the principal.

duties.description: First-class obligations (the 'must'), distinct from the enabling constraints and from the clauses above. Each duty names its bearer. A delegate duty is owed by the agent of record; it is either structured (an effect toward a goal) or prose (a named legal duty). An issuer duty names a governance obligation the issuer accepts. Duties are accountability, not gates -- a stranger-verifier does not gate on them -- so they live here in r, not in a.constraints. Required: every GCD carries the seven baseline duties exactly as the baseline rules state them (timelyReviewAndRevoke, actWithinScope, loyalty, care, confidentiality, keepRecords, escalate), and may add more. A duty may carry custom keys beyond the ones defined here, whose semantics come from the governance framework named in gfw.

oneOf.description: A structured duty the delegate MUST perform: an effect directed toward a goal. Custom keys are allowed, taking their semantics from the governance framework named in gfw; bearer remains a closed const, so an unknown bearer is still rejected. It carries effect and goal and never rule or l, which makes it distinct from the prose shape.

effect.description: The effect the delegate MUST bring about (same axis as constraints.effects).

goal.description: The goal code the duty is directed toward.

cadence.description: Optional description of how often the duty must be performed (free text or an iCalendar RRULE fragment).

priority.description: Precedence for fail-loud conflict resolution: a higher-priority duty outranks a lower one; ties escalate rather than being silently dropped. A conflict involving loyalty, confidentiality or escalate is never resolved by priority and must be referred to the principal.

oneOf.description: A legal duty the delegate MUST perform, stated in prose. It is owed by the agent of record, and by anyone who controls the delegate's keys or directs its acts with notice of these rules (the bindingParties rule). Custom keys are allowed, taking their semantics from the governance framework named in gfw. It carries rule and l and never effect or goal, which makes it distinct from the structured shape.

rule.description: The name of the duty (for example, loyalty).

l.description: Associated legal language stating the duty.

priority.description: Precedence for fail-loud conflict resolution: a higher-priority duty outranks a lower one; ties escalate rather than being silently dropped. A conflict involving loyalty, confidentiality or escalate is never resolved by priority and must be referred to the principal.

oneOf.description: A duty the issuer MUST perform. Custom keys are allowed, taking their semantics from the governance framework named in gfw; bearer remains a closed const, so an unknown bearer is still rejected.

rule.description: The name of a governance rule the issuer accepts as an obligation (for example, timelyReviewAndRevoke).

l.description: Optional associated legal language for the named rule.

priority.description: Precedence for fail-loud conflict resolution: a higher-priority duty outranks a lower one; ties escalate rather than being silently dropped. A conflict involving loyalty, confidentiality or escalate is never resolved by priority and must be referred to the principal.

l.const: Issuers agree to review each delegation they have issued on a cadence appropriate to its stakes, and to revoke or narrow it promptly once the conditions that justified the grant no longer hold. This duty does not extend authority, since a delegation is valid only while its constraints are met, and it creates no liability toward a relying party.
Act only within the constraints of this credential and the principal's lawful instructions.

Act loyally for the principal in all matters connected with this delegation, according to the principal's stated goals and instructions. Do not deal with the principal as an adverse party, act for a party whose interests conflict with the principal's, or obtain a benefit from any party in connection with the principal's affairs, except as the principal consented after disclosure of all material facts.
Act with the care, competence and diligence normally exercised in similar circumstances, and with any special skill that the delegate or the agent of record holds itself out as having.

Use information obtained through this delegation only for the delegated purpose. Do not disclose it except as the delegation requires, and do not combine it with other information to build a profile of the principal beyond what that purpose needs. These rules are not an agreement for the processing of personal data under any data-protection law.

Keep a record of each act taken under this credential sufficient to reconstruct the credential and ancestor identifiers, the disclosure, the acceptance, the act and its time, any required approvals, and the verification and revocation evidence relied on; keep no more than that purpose needs; follow the retention schedule the principal or applicable law sets, but preserve records needed for a reasonably anticipated claim, dispute or legal hold; and give the principal access to them on request.

Before taking an act that involves a conflict of interest not stated in the disclosure, or that a reasonable agent in the delegate's position would recognize as at the edge of this credential's authority, stop and refer it to the principal, and do not proceed until the principal approves by a message it signs that identifies the act. An approval never authorizes an act outside the constraints and cannot confer a reserved power that the reservedPowers constraint does not list. Exercising a listed reserved power within the constraints does not by itself require referral.
